summary: Full daily Power Stack investment refresh. One new diversified resource candidate cleared the quality bar: BHP Group ADR (BHP) at 8.1 after FY2026 results confirmed copper has become its largest earnings engine, while Jansen potash and Olympic Dam uranium by-product exposure add food-security and nuclear crossover. No other new ticker was promoted. Power/Grid remains the core category, but higher long-end yields and oil above $90 increase valuation pressure on long-duration AI and industrial growth names. Water/Cooling remains the strongest newer diversification sleeve. Robotics adoption order is unchanged. July remains the latest official ISM dataset, so the ISM snapshot was re-verified but not rewritten for timestamp-only churn.

macro.rates: The U.S. 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.327%, its highest since 2007, while the 10-year rose to around 4.74%. The main risk to Power Stack is no longer only policy rates: higher term premia, fiscal supply and AI-related corporate borrowing are raising long-duration discount rates.
macro.oil: Brent settled at $91.02 and WTI at $84.94 as U.S.-Iran talks remained stalled and Hormuz traffic stayed constrained. This strengthens integrated energy/refining as a hedge but also raises inflation and financing risk for expensive growth assets.
macro.equities: Technology and semiconductors sold off sharply as yields rose; the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell about 5%. No broad fundamental AI-capex reversal was verified, so this is treated mainly as a valuation/discount-rate warning rather than a thesis break.
macro.metals: Copper remains near record levels amid tight physical supply. BHP's FY2026 results confirm the strategic shift: copper now contributes roughly 55% of underlying EBITDA, overtaking iron ore.

categoryRead.Power / Grid: Still the highest-conviction category. The underlying physical shortage in generation, transmission, substations and switchgear remains intact, but higher long-end yields increase entry-price sensitivity. Prefer visible backlog/order books in GEV, ETN, PWR, HUBB and POWL over generic electrification beta.
categoryRead.AI / Data centres: Positive structurally but under greater valuation scrutiny. Semiconductors and AI-linked shares sold off as yields rose. Keep emphasis on bottlenecks with contracted/visible demand rather than momentum names whose valuation depends on distant cash flows.
categoryRead.Water / Cooling: No ranking change. ECL remains the highest-quality diversified water/cooling exposure, MOD the higher-beta hyperscale thermal-management play and XYL the lower-AI-dependency water infrastructure/reuse compounder.
categoryRead.Nuclear: No core-ranking change. Operating nuclear, BWXT and fuel-cycle scarcity remain preferred for current earnings quality.
categoryRead.Uranium / Fuel: No ranking change after yesterday's NXE promotion. CCJ remains the core producer/services exposure, LEU the strategic U.S. enrichment scarcity play and NXE the higher-beta development-stage satellite. BHP adds indirect uranium optionality through Olympic Dam but is not a replacement for dedicated fuel-cycle exposure.
categoryRead.Oil & Gas: Tactical-positive as both geopolitical hedge and inflation hedge, but high oil is now clearly tightening the broader financial backdrop. Prefer XOM/CVX, gas infrastructure and selective refiners over marginal producers.
categoryRead.Metals: Strengthened. BHP is promoted at 8.1 as a diversified copper/potash/uranium crossover. Copper is now BHP's largest earnings contributor, while potash adds food-security diversification and Olympic Dam adds nuclear optionality.
categoryRead.Robotics / Automation: No hierarchy change: warehouse/fixed automation first, then cobots/mobile manipulation, industrial humanoids, then general-purpose consumer robots. No fresh evidence today justifies promoting a humanoid OEM ahead of SYM/Geekplus/CGNX/TER.
categoryRead.Agriculture / Food Systems: No ranking change. CTVA remains preferred for seed/trait/crop-protection IP; VMI remains the irrigation/grid crossover. BHP's Jansen potash project adds diversified agriculture exposure but does not displace these cleaner operating themes.
categoryRead.Healthcare / Metabolic: No ranking change. LLY and DXCM remain the preferred therapeutics + monitoring pair. Lilly's oral obesity franchise continues to gain momentum, but valuation and franchise concentration still cap conviction.

ism.status: Re-verified; no newer official ISM report exists as of this run.
ism.powerStackRead: Still supportive of physical bottlenecks: manufacturing orders, production and backlog are strong, customers' inventories are very low, while copper, electrical/electronic components, integrated circuits, memory and semiconductors remain constrained. Services demand is resilient but employment is contracting and prices are high, consistent with a high-cost expansion rather than a benign boom.

promotions.reason: FY2026 results materially changed the earnings mix: copper now generates roughly 55% of underlying EBITDA and is BHP's largest contributor. Jansen adds potash/food-security exposure from 2027 and Olympic Dam adds uranium by-product optionality, creating a differentiated cross-category Power Stack holding.

notPromoted: No additional AI, Water/Cooling, Agriculture, Healthcare, Malaysia or Robotics name improved diversification and risk-adjusted quality enough to justify promotion today.
The semiconductor selloff is treated as a valuation/rates warning rather than evidence that AI infrastructure demand has reversed.

liveDesk.read: Live Desk context is available but the AI/Data Centres and Power/Grid theme states are stale/neutral, so no conviction score was mechanically altered from the overlay. AI triggers in Micron/Marvell were noted as research prompts only.

researchGaps: Need a reliable live valuation feed for consistent forward P/E, EV/EBITDA and FCF-yield comparison across every Power Stack name.
Malaysia-listed water-treatment and data-centre cooling exposure remains underdeveloped relative to the U.S. sleeve.
BHP's Jansen potash economics need continued monitoring after impairment/cost overruns; diversification only helps if project returns remain disciplined.
NXE financing structure remains unresolved and should not be treated as funded until terms are announced.
